newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota may suspend output for one day after fire.
newsitem.headline: Toyota may suspend output for one day after fire.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Monday that it may suspend all of its domestic production for one day on Tuesday due to a fire at the weekend at a plant of one of its component suppliers.
A company spokesman said Toyota would restart some of its production lines from Wednesday.
The fire on February 1 at an Aisin Seiki Co Ltd plant halted output of some brake parts supplied to Toyota.
Toyota also said it had decided to drop plans to operate its factories for an extra day next Saturday.
The spokesman said that the impact of the production suspension on the company's earnings was unclear.
According to another Toyota spokesman, the company produces about 14,000 cars per day at its 12 plants in Japan.
He also said that the company had halted operations at its plant on the southern island of Kyushu on Monday.
The company will hold an emergency meeting on Monday afternoon to make a final decision on its production plans.
Earlier, Aisin Seiki said the fire is likely to have caused 1.5 billion yen of damage. The fire destroyed the factory, one of 13 Aisin plants supplying vehicle parts to Toyota.

An Aisin spokesman said the firm would be unable to supply some brake-related products to Toyota as it had not found an alternative production facility. About 90 percent of the company's products are shipped to Toyota, the spokesman said.
